text:
Lena: Quick ping 1 working up a 'strata surgical cutover' playbook for decomposing our monolithic runtime by latency domains (hot/fast, warm, cold). Goal: predictable tech-debt paydown and repeatable migrations.

Omar: love the name. What's the enforcement model for contracts between strata?

Lena: each stratum publishes a minimal RPC surface + async event contract. Contracts live in a contract registry repo and are validated by CI. Service owners must include a compatibility matrix in PRs.

Will (Platform): to add: platform will own the routing shim, health-check shim, and the default fallback pool. We can build a thin adapter so teams don't have to rewrite clients.

Carmen (Eng): real concern: if we split, how do we avoid increased cross-strata chatty calls? That kills latency.

Lena: keep hotpath co-located with caller for first wave. Stratum boundaries should follow call-frequency heatmaps. We'll provide tooling to compute per-endpoint call graphs and recommend boundary candidates.

Omar: what about rollout strategy? feature-flag based? traffic shaping? both?

Lena: both. Traffic shaping at router-level + feature flags at svc-level. We propose 1%/5%/25%/50%/100% canary progression with automated SLO checks at each step.

oncall-bot: oncall-bot: Canary progression started for strata-cutover:v1 -> 1%

Will (Platform): add policy: if error-rate delta > 0.5% absolute OR p95 latency regresses 30% we auto-pause. Also require a manual ack for moving past 25%.

Carmen (Eng): data migration for warm->cold: can we avoid synchronous moves? prefer eventual rehydrate + tombstone strategy.

Lena: yes, prefer lazy-migration + dual-read until parity verified. We'll standardize a reconciliation job that runs at a regular cadence and surfaces mismatch metrics.

Omar: ownership matrix? who owns the recon job infra vs business logic to reconcile?

Will (Platform): platform owns the job scaffolding and infra (k8s job, metrics hooks). Service owner owns reconciliation logic and correctness tests.

Carmen (Eng): tests: we need a small harness to run fuzz workloads against both old and new strata and compare outputs deterministically where possible. Non-deterministic cases get a golden-set differential review.

Lena: agreed. We'll add: unit/contract tests in CI, a harness integration test in infra staging, and a nightly parity sweep during migration windows.

Omar: can we quantify tech-debt reduction? Need KPIs to report progress to execs.

Lena: propose KPIs: number of endpoints moved out of monolith, estimated CPU/GPU cost delta, mean latency improvement on owned hotpaths, and outstanding cross-service coupling score.

Will (Platform): include operational KPIs too: rollback time p95, mean time to detect (MTTD) regression during canary, and canary false-positive rate.

oncall-bot: oncall-bot: Alert threshold set: latency-regression > 30% for 3m -> paging enabled

Carmen (Eng): I'll prototype the call-graph heatmap export and a sample boundary recommendation for the search pipeline.

Lena: awesome. Next steps: I'll open an RFC with the playbook template (contracts, migration phases, CI gates, parity jobs, KPI list). Please comment on owners and thresholds. Plan to roll pilot with search pipeline next sprint.

Omar: happy to pair on the contract registry API.

Will (Platform): I'll stub the routing shim API and on-call playbook snippets.

Carmen (Eng): tagging QA and Observability folks in the RFC.

Lena: thanks team  this should make long-lived refactors less risky and more measurable.
